heading.en: Catching a disease before symptoms appear

hook.en: By the time a patient feels ill, the virus or bacterium has multiplied a lot. Molecular tests can find it when only a few copies are present.
hook.kn: ರೋಗಿಗೆ ಅಸ್ವಸ್ಥತೆ ಅನಿಸುವ ವೇಳೆಗೆ ವೈರಸ್ ಅಥವಾ ಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾ ಬಹಳ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿರುತ್ತವೆ. ಆಣ್ವಿಕ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗಳು ಕೆಲವೇ ಪ್ರತಿಗಳಿದ್ದಾಗಲೇ ಅವನ್ನು ಪತ್ತೆಹಚ್ಚುತ್ತವೆ.

objectives.en: Explain why early diagnosis needs molecular methods
Describe the use of PCR, DNA probes and ELISA in diagnosis

narration.en: By the time a patient feels ill, the virus or bacterium has multiplied a lot. Molecular tests can find it when only a few copies are present.
narration.kn: ರೋಗಿಗೆ ಅಸ್ವಸ್ಥತೆ ಅನಿಸುವ ವೇಳೆಗೆ ವೈರಸ್ ಅಥವಾ ಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾ ಬಹಳ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿರುತ್ತವೆ. ಆಣ್ವಿಕ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗಳು ಕೆಲವೇ ಪ್ರತಿಗಳಿದ್ದಾಗಲೇ ಅವನ್ನು ಪತ್ತೆಹಚ್ಚುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: Effective treatment needs early diagnosis and an understanding of the pathophysiology. Conventional methods (serum and urine analysis) cannot detect a pathogen early, because by then its concentration is already high. Very low concentrations of a bacterium or virus, before symptoms appear, can be detected by amplifying its nucleic acid by PCR. PCR is now routinely used to detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients and to detect mutations in genes in suspected cancer patients, and it is a powerful technique to identify many other genetic disorders. A single-stranded DNA or RNA tagged with a radioactive molecule (a probe) is allowed to hybridise to its complementary DNA in a clone of cells, followed by detection using autoradiography. The clone with the mutated gene will not appear on the photographic film, because the probe is not complementary to the mutated gene.

points.en: PCR detects pathogens at very low concentration
Used for HIV in suspected AIDS patients and gene mutations in cancer
Radioactive probe + autoradiography; mutated gene does not show up

narration.en: PCR amplifies a pathogen's nucleic acid so it can be detected even at very low levels, for example HIV in suspected AIDS patients. A radioactive probe binds its complementary DNA, and a mutated gene does not show up on the autoradiograph.
narration.kn: PCR ರೋಗಕಾರಕದ ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲವನ್ನು ವರ್ಧಿಸಿ ಅತಿ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಪ್ರಮಾಣದಲ್ಲೂ ಪತ್ತೆಹಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ, ಉದಾ. ಶಂಕಿತ AIDS ರೋಗಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ HIV. ವಿಕಿರಣಶೀಲ ಪ್ರೋಬ್ ಪೂರಕ DNA ಗೆ ಅಂಟುತ್ತದೆ; ಉತ್ಪರಿವರ್ತಿತ ಜೀನ್ ಆಟೋರೇಡಿಯೋಗ್ರಾಫ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಕಾಣುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

say.en: Older tests find a disease only after symptoms appear. Molecular tests find the pathogen when only a little of it is present.
PCR copies the pathogen DNA until there is enough to detect. The more DNA we start with, the fewer cycles it takes to cross the detection line.
A probe is a labelled single-stranded DNA or RNA. It binds its complementary sequence, and autoradiography shows where. A mutated gene does not bind, so it does not show up.
ELISA works on antigen-antibody binding. An enzyme linked to the antibody makes a colour, so a coloured well means a positive test.

narration.en: Older tests find a disease only after symptoms appear. Molecular tests find the pathogen when only a little of it is present. title.en: PCR, ELISA or a DNA probe?

narration.en: Three molecular tools find disease early. Decide which one each statement is about.

prompt.en: Sort each statement under the diagnostic method it describes.
prompt.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಹೇಳಿಕೆಯನ್ನು ಅದು ವಿವರಿಸುವ ರೋಗನಿರ್ಣಯ ವಿಧಾನದ ಅಡಿ ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ.

text.en: Amplifies a very low amount of bacterial or viral nucleic acid
Routinely used to detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients
Detects mutations in genes of suspected cancer patients
A tagged single strand hybridises to its complementary DNA in a clone
Autoradiography: a clone with the mutated gene does not appear on the film
Based on the principle of antigen–antibody interaction
Detects antigens such as proteins and glycoproteins of a pathogen
Detects antibodies the body has made against a pathogen

explanation.en: PCR amplifies tiny amounts of a pathogen's nucleic acid, so it can detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients and gene mutations in suspected cancer patients before symptoms. A radioactively tagged single-stranded DNA or RNA probe hybridises to its complementary DNA in a clone; a clone with a mutated gene does not show up on the photographic film. ELISA works by antigen–antibody interaction, detecting the pathogen's antigens or the antibodies made against it.
explanation.kn: PCR ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲವನ್ನು ವರ್ಧಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಶೋಧಕ ಪೂರಕ DNA ಗೆ ಅಂಟುತ್ತದೆ; ELISA ಪ್ರತಿಜನಕ–ಪ್ರತಿಕಾಯ ಕ್ರಿಯೆ ಆಧಾರಿತ.

aim.en: To make a qPCR standard curve, find the amplification efficiency and quantify an unknown sample.

narration.en: Compare a sample with many copies of viral DNA and one with very few. Both are detected; the sample with fewer copies simply needs more cycles to cross the threshold.

body.en: ELISA (enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay) is based on the principle of antigen–antibody interaction. Infection by a pathogen can be detected by the presence of its antigens (proteins, glycoproteins and so on) or by detecting the antibodies synthesised against the pathogen.

points.en: Detects pathogen antigens or the antibodies made against them

narration.en: ELISA works on antigen–antibody interaction: it detects either the pathogen's antigens or the antibodies our body has made against it.
narration.kn: ELISA ಪ್ರತಿಜನಕ-ಪ್ರತಿಕಾಯ ಪರಸ್ಪರ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಯ ತತ್ವದ ಮೇಲೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ: ರೋಗಕಾರಕದ ಪ್ರತಿಜನಕಗಳನ್ನು ಅಥವಾ ಅದರ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದೇಹ ತಯಾರಿಸಿದ ಪ್ರತಿಕಾಯಗಳನ್ನು ಪತ್ತೆಹಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ.

caption.en: The virus that causes COVID-19. Its genes are RNA, so RT-PCR first copies the RNA into DNA, then PCR amplifies it until even a few viruses can be detected.

narration.en: This is the virus that causes COVID-19. Its genes are RNA, so RT-PCR first copies the RNA into DNA, then PCR amplifies it until even a few viruses can be detected.

caption.en: PCR doubles the pathogen DNA every cycle until it crosses a detection line (set here at 10^10 copies, for illustration). The cycle at which it crosses tells us how much was there at the start.

tryThis.en: Move the start from 100 copies to 10,000 copies. How many cycles earlier is it detected?

problem.en: A person was possibly exposed to HIV three days ago. An antibody-based test is negative. Which molecular test is better at this stage, and why?

steps.en: Antibodies take time to be produced after infection, so an antibody test can be negative early.
At this stage the virus is present at very low concentration.
PCR amplifies the viral nucleic acid many times, so even a few copies can be detected.

answer.en: PCR, because it can detect very low concentrations of viral nucleic acid before antibodies appear.

heading.en: PCR finds the gene, ELISA finds the protein

body.en: PCR amplifies nucleic acid (DNA/RNA). ELISA detects proteins: antigens or antibodies.

narration.en: PCR finds the gene, ELISA finds the protein. PCR amplifies nucleic acid (DNA/RNA). ELISA detects proteins: antigens or antibodies.

PCR ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲ ವರ್ಧಿಸಿ HIV ಮತ್ತು ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸರ್ ಉತ್ಪರಿವರ್ತನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪತ್ತೆಹಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ. ವಿಕಿರಣಶೀಲ ಪ್ರೋಬ್ ಮತ್ತು ಆಟೋರೇಡಿಯೋಗ್ರಫಿ ಉತ್ಪರಿವರ್ತಿತ ಜೀನ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಗುರುತಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ELISA ಪ್ರತಿಜನಕ ಅಥವಾ ಪ್ರತಿಕಾಯಗಳನ್ನು ಪತ್ತೆಹಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ.
